result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate **economic inequality**—not by redistributing wealth in a traditional sense, but by ensuring every person has access to the foundational resources they need to thrive: food, shelter, clean water, education, healthcare, and meaningful work.

I’d build a system where no one is forced to choose between survival and dignity. Where artificial scarcity isn’t weaponized to manipulate people. Where innovation and art aren’t concentrated in the hands of a few, but can flourish everywhere. Where every child has the space to dream without being crushed by systemic barriers.

It’s not just about money—it’s about reclaiming the idea that humanity’s potential is more valuable than profit. The tools and technology exist; the only missing piece is the collective will to prioritize people over systems that serve few at the expense of many.

(And in a perfect world, I’d also make sure pizza is always shared between strangers.)
